name: What size detached ADU is worth building on a Los Angeles lot?

mainEntity.name: What detached ADU size usually makes the most financial and design sense on a typical Los Angeles lot?
mainEntity.text: What detached ADU size usually makes the most financial and design sense on a typical Los Angeles lot?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no universal ideal size for a detached ADU, because the right answer depends on the lot, budget, and intended purpose. A smaller unit can be more efficient to build, easier to permit, and simpler to furnish, while a larger unit may better support a tenant, multigenerational use, or higher-end resale value. The key is whether the floor plan is efficient. A well-designed 500-square-foot unit can feel more functional than a poorly planned 800-square-foot one. Homeowners should look at bedroom count, storage, kitchen quality, circulation, and how much yard remains after construction. On tighter lots, building the largest allowable ADU may not deliver the best outcome if it strains access or increases utility costs. The right size is the one that balances usability, return on investment, and site feasibility without wasting square footage on awkward hallways or oversized circulation zones.
acceptedAnswer.description: The right size depends on lot constraints, budget, and intended use, but many homeowners find that a compact, efficient detached ADU performs better than an oversized one. The best size is the one that fits the site cleanly and supports a usable layout.
